title: The Age of the Patriarchs
lead: Genesis 12–50 tells of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and their wives, Israel's "fathers." When, and whether, they lived is one of the most debated questions in biblical history: traditional readers place them in the early second millennium BC, while many critical scholars see the stories as shaped in the first millennium.

sections.h: The fathers in the rest of the Bible
sections.b: Later books treat Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as the founders of the covenant: God "remembered his covenant, the one with Abraham, with Isaac and with Jacob" (Exodus 2:24), Joshua retells their story from Terah onward (Joshua 24:2–4), and the Psalms sing of the promise to them (Psalm 105:8–15). The New Testament speaks of "the God of our fathers" (Acts 3:13) and of the patriarchs living as foreigners in tents while waiting for a city with foundations (Hebrews 11:8–16).
